sentences.en: Hey, gang.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome to SmartLiSt. We are a sweet new podcast starring myself, Sean Hayes, Jason Bateman, and Will Arnett, and we are complete idiots.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听 SmartLess。我们是一档非常棒的新播客，由我肖恩·海耶斯、杰森·贝特曼和威尔·阿奈特共同主持，我们全都是十足的笨蛋。

sentences.en: So what we do is we bring on a guest and we ask them stuff and they make us smarter.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的节目形式是，邀请一位嘉宾来，问他们各种问题，然后他们让我们变得更聪明。

sentences.en: Hopefully.
sentences.zh: 希望如此。

sentences.en: It's super cool.
sentences.zh: 这节目太酷了。

sentences.en: So please, come with us.
sentences.zh: 所以请和我们一起来吧。

sentences.en: Enjoy the show.
sentences.zh: 好好享受节目。

sentences.en: Okay, so welcome to SmartLiSt. Now, Jason, today's guest is your guest, Stacey Abrams, but we recorded this a while ago.
sentences.zh: 好的，欢迎来到 SmartLess。杰森，今天的嘉宾是你的嘉宾斯泰西·艾布拉姆斯，不过我们是不久前录制的。

sentences.en: So could you just give us a little bit of a timeline on Stacey's interview and why she's airing now?
sentences.zh: 所以你能简单给我们讲讲斯泰西这期采访的时间线，以及为什么现在才播出吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, we recorded this a few weeks ago and we wanted to hold it so that we could release it a little bit closer to Election Day because of the ground that we cover.
sentences.zh: 对，我们几周前录的，当时想压一阵子，好在离选举日近一点的时候发出来，因为我们聊的内容。

sentences.en: You know, we talk about voter suppression and, you know, the election in general, et cetera, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们聊到了选民压制，还有大选本身之类的各种话题。

sentences.en: So the stuff that we don't talk about has not happened or did not happen.
sentences.zh: 所以我们没聊到的那些事，当时还没发生。

sentences.en: Right, because a lot has happened, right, in that time?
sentences.zh: 对，因为这段时间发生了好多事，对吧？

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So apologies for stuff not mentioned, but the future had not happened yet.
sentences.zh: 所以对于没有提到的事情，先道个歉，因为未来还没发生呢。

sentences.en: So enjoy the episode.
sentences.zh: 那么请欣赏本期节目。

sentences.en: Here comes.
sentences.zh: 要来啦。

sentences.en: Guys, we've got a respectable guest with us today.
sentences.zh: 伙计们，我们今天迎来了重量级嘉宾。

sentences.en: And I'm not going to bore anybody with a bunch of intro nonsense because she need none.
sentences.zh: 我可不想用一堆废话开场来烦大家，因为她根本不需要。

sentences.en: Ladies and gentlemen, Stacey AbraMs.
sentences.zh: 女士们先生们，斯泰西·艾布拉姆斯。

sentences.en: Whoa.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇哦。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好啦。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 行啦。

sentences.en: Oh, my gosh.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: What an honor.
sentences.zh: 太荣幸了。

sentences.en: This is so cool.
sentences.zh: 这太酷了。

sentences.en: Tighten up, man.
sentences.zh: 收敛点，老兄。

sentences.en: Okay?
sentences.zh: 好吗？

sentences.en: Look at you.
sentences.zh: 看看你。

sentences.en: Well done, Jason.
sentences.zh: 干得漂亮，杰森。

sentences.en: What a gueSt.
sentences.zh: 多棒的嘉宾啊。

sentences.en: I'm such a huge fan of yours.
sentences.zh: 我是你的超级粉丝。

sentences.en: This is so cool to meet you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能见到你。

sentences.en: Oh, Stacey, this is great to meet you.
sentences.zh: 哦，斯泰西，很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: Well, likewise.
sentences.zh: 彼此彼此。

sentences.en: I'm fangirling internally.
sentences.zh: 我内心正疯狂追星呢。

sentences.en: Jason can tell you I can do an IMDb on all of you.
sentences.zh: 杰森可以告诉你，你们每个人的演艺履历我都倒背如流。

sentences.en: So I watch a lot of television.
sentences.zh: 所以我看很多电视。

sentences.en: I did have a brief conversation with her about a week ago, and she was very, very, very nice.
sentences.zh: 我大约一周前和她简单聊过，她人真的非常好、非常、非常好。

sentences.en: I was surprised.
sentences.zh: 我很吃惊。

sentences.en: I'm always surprised that anybody knows who the heck I am.
sentences.zh: 每当有人居然知道我是个什么东西时，我总是很惊讶。

sentences.en: It is one of the few good things about being kind of pseudo-famous is that you can kind of cut through the first 12 questions,
sentences.zh: 成为这种半红不紫的名人，为数不多的好处之一就是，你可以直接跳过前十二个问题，

sentences.en: and you get right into kind of a conversation with someone like at a peer level, and you just get right into it.
sentences.zh: 然后就像同行一样直接开始深入交流，切入正题。

sentences.en: It's a nice—
sentences.zh: 这真是一件——

sentences.en: Right, because they're not going like, Jason, now what do you do?
sentences.zh: 对，因为他们不会问：杰森，你现在到底是干什么的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: You haven't had that in a minute.
sentences.zh: 你有一阵子没这样了。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Well, Stacey, I'm really not sure where to begin.
sentences.zh: 嗯，斯泰西，我真不知道该从哪里说起。

sentences.en: And obviously, you're doing the country an enormous service with the amount of work you're doing on giving people the sense or the reality, hopefully,
sentences.zh: 显然，你为这个国家作出了巨大的贡献，通过你所做的大量工作，让人们感觉到，或者说希望成为现实，

sentences.en: that all their votes are going to count.
sentences.zh: 那就是他们的每一票都会算数。

sentences.en: And for our single listener out there who is not that bright, they're as smartless as we are.
sentences.zh: 对于我们那位不太聪明的唯一的听众，他们跟我们一样没那么聪明。

sentences.en: That's why they tune in.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们收听节目的原因。

sentences.en: They want to get less dumb.
sentences.zh: 他们想变得不那么蠢。

sentences.en: Can you give them a brief explanation about what your primary focus is every morning now that you're getting up and trying to push the ball forward in this main area of trying to eliminate voter suppression?
sentences.zh: 你能给他们简要解释一下，你每天早晨醒来、试图在消除选民压制这个主要领域推动进展时，你的核心重点是什么吗？

sentences.en: How can they feel better about the possibilities of that today?
sentences.zh: 他们今天怎么能对这方面的可能性感觉好一点呢？

sentences.en: How many hours do I have?
sentences.zh: 我有多少时间？

sentences.en: You've got all the time you want on this.
sentences.zh: 在这件事上你有的是时间。

sentences.en: We have nothing left to do today.
sentences.zh: 我们今天无事可做了。

sentences.en: You're it.
sentences.zh: 就靠你了。

sentences.en: So, first of all, thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 那么，首先，非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: This is a delight.
sentences.zh: 这太令人高兴了。

sentences.en: Voter suppression is basically when you are prevented from or discouraged from voting.
sentences.zh: 选民压制基本上是指你被阻止或被劝阻去投票。

sentences.en: Typically, it is practiced by an instrument of the government, like, oh, let's say, a secretary of state running for governor against you as an opponent.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，它是通过政府机构来实施的，比如，哦，比方说，一个正在竞选州长、而你正是其竞争对手的国务卿。

sentences.en: Or...
sentences.zh: 或者……

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: Off the top of my head, that's one example.
sentences.zh: 我想到的就是这样一个例子。

sentences.en: Or it can be a U.S.
sentences.zh: 或者可能是美国

sentences.en: Supreme Court telling you that you have to go and vote in the middle of a pandemic if you live in Wisconsin or Texas or Alabama.
sentences.zh: 最高法院告诉你，如果你住在威斯康星州、得克萨斯州或阿拉巴马州，在大流行期间你也必须去投票。

sentences.en: Anyway, so voter suppression is when there is an attempt made to throttle your ability to vote.
sentences.zh: 总之，所以选民压制就是有人企图扼杀你投票的能力。

sentences.en: The challenge is that in the 21st century,
sentences.zh: 面临的挑战是，在21世纪，

sentences.en: most voter suppression activities have been perpetrated by Republicans because they find themselves on the losing end of an expansion of who can participate in our democracy.
sentences.zh: 大多数选民压制活动都是由共和党人犯下的，因为他们发现自己处于扩大民主参与度这一潮流的劣势方。

sentences.en: And so, typically, the strongest predictor of political leanings is race, which means that whether they think they're racist or not,
sentences.zh: 因此，通常情况下，政治倾向最强的预测指标是种族，这意味着无论他们认为自己是否种族主义者，

sentences.en: most of the voter suppression actions are targeted at people of color because we are the most likely to vote Democratic.
sentences.zh: 大多数选民压制行动都是针对有色人种的，因为我们最有可能投给民主党。

sentences.en: Their second favorite target are students, and that's why you find voter suppression across the country, but why you find it in, you know, New Hampshire,
sentences.zh: 他们第二喜欢的靶子是学生，这就是为什么你会在全国各地发现选民压制，也是为什么你会在，你知道的，新罕布什尔州发现这一点，

sentences.en: where they passed a law to try to disenfranchise student voters.
sentences.zh: 在那里他们通过了一项法律，试图剥夺学生选民的选举权。

sentences.en: And then the last thing I'll say is this.
sentences.zh: 然后我要说的最后一点是这个。

sentences.en: The architecture of voter suppression is the same no matter where you live.
sentences.zh: 无论你住在哪里，选民压制的架构都是一样的。

sentences.en: It's, do they make it hard for you to register and stay on the rolls?
sentences.zh: 那就是，他们是不是让你很难注册并留在选民名册上？

sentences.en: Do they make it hard for you to cast a ballot?
sentences.zh: 他们是不是让你很难投出一张选票？

sentences.en: Meaning, do they make it hard for you to get an absentee ballot?
sentences.zh: 也就是说，他们是不是让你很难拿到缺席选票？

sentences.en: Do they make it hard for you to get to a polling place because they shut it down?
sentences.zh: 他们是不是因为关闭了投票站而让你很难去投票？

sentences.en: They moved it and didn't tell you.
sentences.zh: 他们搬迁了投票站却不告诉你。

sentences.en: And then the third is, does your ballot count what I like to refer to as Florida?
sentences.zh: 然后第三点是，你的选票算数吗？我喜欢把这称作“佛罗里达现象”。

sentences.en: So it is.
sentences.zh: 所以就是这样。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So it's, it's basically, and it looks different from state to state because we do not have a single democracy in America.
sentences.zh: 所以，它基本上是这样的，而且在不同州表现各不相同，因为我们在美国没有单一的民主制度。

sentences.en: We've got 50 different iterations where each state gets to decide how to administer elections.
sentences.zh: 我们有50种不同的运作方式，每个州都可以自行决定如何管理选举。

sentences.en: The Constitution says you have the right to vote, but it delegated to each state the ability to administer the vote.
sentences.zh: 宪法规定你有投票权，但它将管理投票的权力下放给了每个州。

sentences.en: And so we have voter suppression because bad actors get worse.
sentences.zh: 所以我们之所以存在选民压制，是因为坏坏得更彻底。

sentences.en: Good actors sometimes stay okay.
sentences.zh: 好人有时能勉强保持正直。

sentences.en: And folks who are in the middle look to see if they can win or lose depending on what they do.
sentences.zh: 而处于中间立场的人则在观望，看自己根据所作所为是会赢还是会输。

sentences.en: And they tend towards voter suppression.
sentences.zh: 他们往往倾向于选民压制。

sentences.en: I'm a bad actor, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想我算是个坏人吧。

sentences.en: I feel like when you said bad actor, you looked at Sean too.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你刚才说“演技差”的时候，也看了一眼肖恩。

sentences.en: Yeah, definitely.
sentences.zh: 对，绝对是的。

sentences.en: So let's, you won't say this, so I'll say it.
sentences.zh: 所以，你不会说这个，那我来好了。

sentences.en: They were obviously successful in what they tried to do in the gubernatorial race.
sentences.zh: 他们在州长竞选中尝试做的事情，显然成功了。

sentences.en: In Georgia.
sentences.zh: 在佐治亚州。

sentences.en: In Georgia, in other words, they knocked a ton of people off that, that would definitely have voted for you.
sentences.zh: 在佐治亚州，换句话说，他们剔除了大量肯定会投给你的人。

sentences.en: You lost by 50,000.
sentences.zh: 你输了五万票。

sentences.en: They knocked what over a million, almost 2 million people off the rolls, right?
sentences.zh: 他们把超过一百万、快两百万的人从选民名册上划掉了，对吧？

sentences.en: 1.4 million were purged over time.
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移，有140万被清洗掉了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, so, so they were successful there, which is horrific.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以，所以他们在那里成功了，这太可怕了。

sentences.en: Can we feel confident that were that race to be run today, that wouldn't happen again?
sentences.zh: 如果我们现在重新进行那场竞选，我们能有信心那种事不会再次发生吗？

sentences.en: Have you been successful at least locally there?
sentences.zh: 你们至少在当地取得成功了吗？

sentences.en: And if the answer is yes, have you been able, do you get the sense that you've been successful in other states as well,
sentences.zh: 如果答案是肯定的，你们觉得在其他州也取得了成功吗？

sentences.en: such that we have less to worry about now than we did back then?
sentences.zh: 以至于我们现在比当时需要担心的事情要少？

sentences.en: I would say we have different things to worry about, but it's getting better.
sentences.zh: 我想说，我们需要担心的事情不一样了，但情况正在变好。

sentences.en: So there are two ways to, to tackle voter suppression.
sentences.zh: 所以解决选民压制问题有两个途径。

sentences.en: One is by actually making the laws work for voters, which is my preference.
sentences.zh: 一个是真正让法律为选民服务，这也是我的首选。

sentences.en: And so in Georgia, for example, we face this thing called exact match.
sentences.zh: 所以在佐治亚州，举个例子，我们面临着一个叫作“严格匹配”的东西。

sentences.en: In 2018, 53,000 people had their applications to register to vote held hostage by the secretary of state.
sentences.zh: 在2018年，有5万3千人的选民登记申请被州务卿扣为人质。

sentences.en: 80% of them were people of color.
sentences.zh: 其中80%是有色人种。

sentences.en: 70% were black people.
sentences.zh: 70%是黑人。

sentences.en: We have been able to make strides in reducing the effectiveness of exact match and purging and basically stopping voters.
sentences.zh: 我们已经取得了进展，削弱了严格匹配和清洗选民的效力，基本上阻止了这种剥夺选民权利的做法。

sentences.en: In 2019, the secretary of state attempted to purge 309,000 people.
sentences.zh: 在2019年，州务卿企图清洗30万9千人。

sentences.en: We were able to save 22,000 by pointing out that he was doing it wrong.
sentences.zh: 我们通过指出他的错误，成功挽救了2万2千人。

sentences.en: We got another few thousand to reassert their right to vote.
sentences.zh: 我们还让另外几千人重新确立了他们的投票权。

sentences.en: And there was a law that was passed that did not apply for some godforsaken reason to this group.
sentences.zh: 有一项通过的法律，不知出于什么鬼理由，没有适用于这群人。

sentences.en: But going forward, you have more time before you get kicked off the rolls.
sentences.zh: 但往前看，在你被踢出名册之前，你有了更多的时间。

sentences.en: So Georgia is getting slowly better, but they have new ways to do stupid and incompetent.
sentences.zh: 所以佐治亚州正在慢慢变好，但他们又有了表现愚蠢和无能的新花样。

sentences.en: So when you saw the June 9th election, that was sort of a replay of their greatest hits of voter suppression.
sentences.zh: 所以当你看到6月9日的选举时，那有点像他们精选的“选民压制最佳金曲”重播。

sentences.en: And they added on top of it the purchase of $100 million worth of machines that didn't work in most counties.
sentences.zh: 而且他们在此之上，还采购了价值1亿美元、在多数县都无法正常工作的机器。

sentences.en: And thus, you had elections that took a long time.
sentences.zh: 因此，你们经历的选举耗费了很长时间。

sentences.en: And so my point is, part of the reason for the work we do is that we've got to figure out for each election what the suppression looks like.
sentences.zh: 所以我的意思是，我们开展这项工作的部分原因在于，我们必须弄清楚每次选举中压制选民的手段是什么样子的。

sentences.en: But using the primaries helps us get prepared for the general.
sentences.zh: 但利用初选有助于我们为大选做好准备。

sentences.en: It's like the dress rehearsal.
sentences.zh: 这就像是彩排。

sentences.en: And so we know both in Georgia and around the country what is going to happen, what's going to go wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以无论是在佐治亚州还是全国各地，我们都知道将要发生什么，什么地方会出问题。

sentences.en: We know that in Nevada, the Republican Secretary of State shut down every single precinct except for one per county.
sentences.zh: 我们知道在内华达州，共和党州务卿关闭了每一个投票站，除了每个县只留一个。

sentences.en: Except in the county where Las Vegas is located, 80% of Nevadans live in that county.
sentences.zh: 除了拉斯维加斯所在的那个县，80%的内华达人住在那个县。

sentences.en: So it's kind of problematic.
sentences.zh: 所以这就有点问题了。

sentences.en: But we know that.
sentences.zh: 但我们知道这一点。

sentences.en: So we can either file a lawsuit about it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们要么可以就此提起诉讼。

sentences.en: We can try to negotiate with the secretaries of state or local elections officials.
sentences.zh: 我们可以尝试与州务卿或地方选举官员进行协商。

sentences.en: There's a lot that can be done now that we know what's wrong.
sentences.zh: 既然我们知道了问题所在，现在有很多事情可以做。

sentences.en: And the work that we do through Fair Fight has been getting in there to mitigate the harm during the primaries,
sentences.zh: 我们通过“公平战斗”（Fair Fight）开展的工作一直在介入其中，以减轻初选期间的损害，

sentences.en: but also use the primaries to gather stories and evidence so that we can be prepared for November.
sentences.zh: 同时也利用初选收集故事和证据，以便我们能为11月做好准备。

sentences.en: And I'm hopeful that November will be better.
sentences.zh: 我希望11月会更好。

sentences.en: I mean, wow.
sentences.zh: 我是说，哇。

sentences.en: First of all, that's so chilling, of course, right?
sentences.zh: 首先，这太让人不寒而栗了，当然，对吧？

sentences.en: And all of it, any kind of sort of voter suppression is chilling when we look at it now.
sentences.zh: 而且所有这些，任何形式的选民压制，当我们现在回头看时，都让人不寒而栗。

sentences.en: Obviously, it's been going on for a long, long time.
sentences.zh: 显然，这种情况已经持续了很久很久。

sentences.en: And it must be frustrating just making these small dents in it, but continuing on.
sentences.zh: 而且，面对现状只能取得这些微小的进展，却还要咬牙坚持，一定很令人沮丧。

sentences.en: And my question is, is this something – what I wonder, what scares me is,
sentences.zh: 我的问题是，这算是一件……我所疑惑的、让我感到害怕的是，

sentences.en: is this something that has just gone on sort of unsaid amongst the people who are perpetrating this suppression?
sentences.zh: 这是一种在实施这种压制的人群中秘而不宣、心照不宣的事情吗？

sentences.en: Or is there an actual – do you think that there's actual dialogue that happens where they coordinate?
sentences.zh: 还是说——你认为他们实际上有过具体的对话，并在其中进行了协调？
